response.query: Which gold-standard methods and sample sizes will we use to estimate sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of the error classification beyond kappa?
response.answer: For estimating sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV, use large sample sizes and gold-standard reference methods. Generally, a minimum of 200 samples is recommended for reliable estimates. Partial verification studies can also be used when full verification is impractical.

results.title: Reporting Results from Studies Evaluating Diagnostic Tests
results.content: If you determine that using a reference standard on all subjects is impractical or not feasible, FDA recommends you obtain estimates of sensitivity and specificity using the new test and a comparative method (other than a reference standard) on all subjects, and use the reference standard on just a subset of subjects (sometimes called partial verification studies or two-stage studies). Usually, to estimate sensitivity and specificity, the outcome of the new test is compared to the reference standard using subjects who are representative of the intended use (both condition present and condition absent) population. Example of results comparing new test A to a non-reference standard for 572 subjects where the positive percent agreement is low, but overall agreement is high**. Example of results comparing new test B to a non-reference standard for 572 subjects where the positive percent agreement is high, and overall agreement is high**.
